title: Structured logging for Node services
when: A server or script logs with scattered console.log calls and the user wants logs that can be searched and filtered.
inputs: the service and its main operations
prompt:
Goal: One small logger writing one JSON object per line with time, level, message and context, correlated by request id.
Steps:
1. Write log.js exporting a logger with debug, info, warn and error that writes JSON.stringify({ time, level, msg, ...fields }) plus newline to stdout (errors to stderr).
2. Use new Date().toISOString() for time and a stable message string; put variable data in fields, not in msg.
3. Serialize errors as { name, message, stack, code } since JSON.stringify(err) gives {}.
4. Create child loggers with bound context: log.child({ requestId, route }) at the start of each request.
5. Generate requestId with crypto.randomUUID() or read an incoming X-Request-Id, and echo it in the response header.
6. Log one line per request at the end with status and duration in ms.
Quality bar:
- Every line is valid JSON.
- Messages are constant so they can be grouped.
- No log call inside tight loops.
Pitfalls:
- Building messages with template strings that hide fields.
- Logging whole request bodies.
- Writing logs with sync file calls per request.
Verify:
- [ ] Each log line parses as JSON.
- [ ] Errors include stack and message.
- [ ] Request lines carry requestId and duration.
- [ ] Files parse.
Output: log.js and the call sites switched to it.
